question: What is our refreshed verdict on ASE Technology after Pass 1 forensic discoveries and the Nov 20 Stage 4 stop breach?

epigraph.quote: Underwrite the business first, verify cash conversion and footnotes second, and never negotiate with a broken stop on the tape.
epigraph.author: Institutional Research Desk

web_blocks.html: ASE Technology Holding Co., Ltd. (NYSE: ASX) is the world's largest outsourced semiconductor assembly and test (OSAT) provider (~27–28% share) alongside its USI EMS/SiP unit [4, 10]. In FY2025, ASE generated NT$645.39 billion in revenue (~$20.8 billion) [4, 5]. Its LEAP advanced packaging line is scaling from ~$1.6 billion in FY2025 toward >$4.0 billion in FY2026 [3]. That mix shift lifted Q3 2026 sales +44.8% YoY to NT$244.16 billion, ATM gross margin to 30.6%, and October sales +47.1% YoY to NT$88.62 billion [1, 27]. Yet Pass 1 forensics uncovered -NT$115.9 billion in 9M 2026 FCF and a +53.9% debt surge to NT$406.5 billion [28, 29]. Management also guided 2027 CapEx above $11.5B amid Nov 18 BIS export curbs, 25% top-client reliance, and rising 2027–2028 rivals [3, 30, 33, 37].

web_blocks.takeaway: We exit all 82 Schwab shares immediately after the $29.25 stop breach, reject new capital (TIER_0) on TREND, CASH_FLOW, and VALUATION ($16.47 Base fair value vs. $26.27 CMP), move ASX to Discarded, and keep 100% of freed cash in USD reserves.

web_blocks.html: This refresh shows why separating business underwriting from valuation math and tape rules protects capital. ASE's engineers are executing well on AI packaging. However, an $11.5 billion CapEx wave—with 2027 guided higher—pushed 9M debt up NT$140.9 billion [3, 6, 28]. That buildout collided with Nov 18 BIS export rules, a reconciled $1.22 FY27E EPS bridge, and a market Downtrend [22, 33]. At $26.27—below our $29.25 hard stop and above our $16.47 Base value—we exit all 82 shares cleanly and wait in cash until a $14–$16 Stage 1 base and positive FCF return.

book_paragraphs: Welcome to our refreshed, ground-up underwriting of ASE Technology Holding—NYSE ticker ASX—as of the November 20, 2026 close. A week ago, ASX traded at $35.55 in a Stage 3 pullback, and we held 82 Schwab shares with an ironclad $29.25 hard stop while keeping new capital on the sidelines.

What happened over the next five sessions shows why pre-committed risk rules and independent P&L checks exist. First, our blind Pass 1 re-audit uncovered critical facts inside ASE's Q3 2026 Form 6-K, FY2025 Form 20-F footnotes, and November 18 U.S. export notices: nine-month free cash flow swung to negative NT$115.9 billion, total interest-bearing debt surged 53.9 percent to NT$406.5 billion, single-customer concentration stood at 25.0 percent, external substrate reliance stood at 91.3 percent, and USI's EMS mix remained 41 percent Consumer and only 6 percent Automotive.

Then on November 20, 2026, the stock broke down violently—falling 13.84 percent in a single day on 2.13x volume to close at $26.27, nearly 10.2 percent below our $29.25 stop. That close confirms Weinstein Stage 4 markdown, sitting 23.7 percent beneath the 200-day moving average and 34.8 percent beneath the 50-day moving average inside a ten-distribution-day S&P 500 Downtrend.

Our refreshed dual verdict is direct and unhedged. For the 82 shares held in Schwab ($2,154.14 market value, -13.85 percent unrealized loss), the action is EXIT_IMMEDIATELY—honoring our breached $29.25 stop at market open without waiting for a bounce. For new capital, the verdict shifts to REJECTED (TIER_0) on TREND, CASH_FLOW, and VALUATION grounds, moving ASX off the active Shortlist to the Discarded bench.

Across the ten chapters that follow, you will read both the genuine engineering strength inside ASE's LEAP packaging lines (Chapters 1 through 5) and the hard balance-sheet, reconciled earnings ($1.22 FY27E EPS), and competitive realities (Chapters 6 through 9) that govern our $16.47 Base fair value, $12.00 bear floor, $28.00 bull ceiling, and 100 percent USD cash redeployment plan.

book_subsections.title: What Changed Between November 13 and November 20, 2026
paragraphs: Three major updates transformed this underwriting in seven days. First, Q3 2026 cash-flow and balance-sheet footnotes showed that funding $11.5 billion of FY2026 CapEx pushed net debt-to-equity to 0.66x and lifted quarterly net interest expense to NT$2.61 billion ahead of a 2027 debt maturity wall, while CFO Joseph Tung warned 2027 CapEx will be larger still. Second, reconciling FY2027E earnings ($30.2 billion revenue at 12.2 percent OPM across 2.22 billion ADS shares equals $1.22 EPS) and capping the Base multiple at 13.5x (below TSMC's 13.81x) lowered our Base fair value to $16.47.

Third, the price tape broke down 27.2 percent in one week to $26.27, breaching our $29.25 hard stop on double volume. Instead of moving the stop lower or hiding behind a vague watch label, this dossier enforces full exit execution, reclassifies ASX to Discarded, and keeps 100 percent of freed proceeds in USD cash.

book_subsections.title: How to Read This Refreshed Monograph Without Anchoring Bias
paragraphs: One of the hardest habits in investing is letting go of last week's price target when new balance-sheet and tape evidence arrives. When we reviewed ASE Technology on November 13, 2026, shares closed at $35.55 above the 200-day moving average. Seven days later, two forces changed our underwriting simultaneously: first, a verdict-stripped audit of the Q3 2026 Form 6-K and FY2025 Form 20-F footnotes revealed negative NT$115.9 billion nine-month free cash flow, a 53.9 percent surge in debt to NT$406.5 billion, 25.0 percent single-customer reliance, 91.3 percent external substrate dependence, and November 18 U.S. BIS export restrictions; second, the stock crashed 13.84 percent on November 20 to $26.27, breaking our $29.25 hard stop while reconciled valuation math placed Base value at $16.47.

Rather than clinging to stale assumptions, this refreshed monograph starts fresh from the factory floor up, keeps every engineering achievement in Chapters 1 through 5 intact, and updates Chapters 6 through 9 without confirmation bias. As you read or listen, notice how every decision traces directly to a documented number or chart level—never a gut feeling.

book_callouts.title: NARRATOR'S REFLECTION
book_callouts.text: Good companies do not always make good stocks at peak CapEx. When negative NT$115.9B of nine-month cash burn and a $16.47 Base fair value meet Stage 4 price action and a breached $29.25 stop, disciplined investors exit immediately and keep 100% of the proceeds in cash.
